items.title: Farrer result turns One Nation from protest to genuine electoral threat
items.description: The result in Farrer has made One Nation’s attempts to become the natural home for conservative Australians look less like a protest and more like a genuine electoral threat.

items.title: We asked the IRGC for their Strait of Hormuz rules and they emailed us back
items.description: Amid a fragile ceasefire between the US and Iran, the IRGC has launched a maritime authority for the Strait of Hormuz. The Persian Gulf Strait Authority says ships need to email their application for passage. So, we sent them a request.

items.title: We're living in the age of exhaustion. Who pays the price of burnout?
items.description: Burnout is everywhere — in resignation letters, therapy sessions and late-night emails. Yet the debate over what it is reveals a bigger question: Should workplaces bear responsibility for the damage modern work can cause?

items.title: Top-earning Australians make money very differently from typical workers
items.description: In Australia, the way people earn their money affects the rate of tax they pay — and top earners have a very different income mix from everyone else.

items.title: Live: Iran's IRGC threatens US sites as Trump awaits Tehran response
items.description: Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps has threatened to target US sites if its tankers come under fire, Iranian media is reporting. It comes as Washington continues to wait for Tehran's response to its latest negotiating position. Follow live.

items.title: Who is responsible for the problems in Alice Springs town camps?
items.description: Conditions in town camps in Alice Springs are under intense scrutiny, but the residents are caught in a tangled web of bureaucracy with little transparency on the money being spent and who exactly is responsible for what.

items.title: John Polson was headed for jail. One phone call changed his life forever
items.description: John Polson was a troubled teen when a sliding doors moment led him into the world of acting. He went on to create Tropfest, one of the world's biggest short film festivals, changing his life and the Australian industry.

items.title: The 'barrier' that must be removed before landmark Defence inquiry
items.description: The impending military sexual violence inquiry is a time for Defence to "reckon with" its past. But advocates say it will be half-baked unless defence lifts gag orders on victims ahead of hearings.

items.title: How Nigel Farage went from outsider to contender for UK PM
items.description: Nigel Farage has his eye on the prime minister's job himself and, if Reform can sustain this level of support at a general election, the keys to Downing Street may fall to him.

items.title: Councils to get federal funds for roads, pipes and wires in housing push
items.description: Treasurer Jim Chalmers will reveal details of the $2 billion fund in Tuesday's federal budget, declaring the cash injection will add an extra 65,000 homes over a decade.

items.title: Vine out of Giro after horrific crash, director called 'scared dog' by riders
items.description: Jay Vine's awful luck continued on stage two of the Giro d'Italia with the Australian taken to hospital following a horror crash on wet roads that saw multiple riders abandon the race.

items.title: Australian cafe owner looking to protect signature drink from imitators
items.description: Melbourne cafe owner Caleb Cha is looking into how he can legally stop shops in Indonesia from imitating his signature Tiger Bomb coffee.

items.title: The 'magnificent' mansion that housed movie stars, hippies and refugees
items.description: From post-war Jewish refugees, who arrived with nothing but hope, to the bohemian artists and performers who took over in the 1970s, historic Melbourne mansion Labassa has more stories than rooms.

items.title: Whale disposal scrutinised after boat ramp 'debacle' attracts sharks
items.description: Marine scientists want to see whale carcasses towed offshore and disposed of out to sea in a process they say is safer, cheaper and more ecologically friendly.

items.title: Step away from the spellcheck. It’s quiz time
items.description: Ready to hone your homophones and verbalise your vowels? Let's get spelling!

items.title: Singer Kira Puru was 'immediately humbled' on first acting job
items.description: Kira Puru is known for their triple j Hottest 100-charting energetic pop music, but this year the musician has roles in not one, but two of the biggest Australian TV shows. What's behind the pivot?

items.title: Protests, nudity and prime ministerial heat: 25 years of Big Brother
items.description: Imported to Australia 25 years ago, Big Brother introduced the country to the concept of 24-hour monitoring as entertainment.

items.title: 'Easy to get influenced': What cheaper weight-loss drugs means for millions
items.description: India has become one of the first countries to introduce cheaper, generic brands of weight loss drugs like Ozempic and Wegovy, but health professionals warn a lack of regulation and oversight is causing problems.

items.title: The RBA's post-COVID rate hikes caused Australians to work more
items.description: The International Monetary Fund found that thousands of Australians took on a second or third job when the RBA hiked rates rapidly in 2022 and 2023. It expected the opposite.

items.title: Ancient winegrape variety reducing farmers' water consumption by 75pc
items.description: In an Australian first, two South Australian winegrape growers are trialling an ancient variety from Cyprus that is reducing water consumption and reconnecting them to their Mediterranean roots.

items.title: Women's players sick of being told 'don't bite the hand that feeds you'
items.description: Players from various codes across the country will protest gender-based violence and call for greater accountability from clubs when instances of mistreatment arise.

items.title: Cats spoil Magpies' party as concussion floors Moore, Suns down Saints in Darwin
items.description: A huge collision sees Darcy Moore concussed as Geelong takes control against Collingwood at the MCG as Gold Coast downs St Kilda in Darwin with star defender Cal Wilkie injured.

items.title: Ponga stunned as Queensland left 'shattered' by Dearden Origin blow
items.description: Newcastle Knights captain Kalyn Ponga was left stunned after his side's big win over St George Illawarra, being told Queensland will be without halfback Tom Dearden for State of Origin.

items.title: The invisible problem sitting under Queensland streets and homes
items.description: At least 22,000km of water mains in Queensland's network are headed towards the end of their useful life span, leading to an "infrastructure cliff".

items.title: WA teens say anonymous 'alt' accounts used to bypass social media ban
items.description: Teenagers in Western Australia's north are calling for better social media regulation to prevent "alt" accounts from spreading malicious content.
